newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Strike hits Manila waterworks on fears of job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Strike hits Manila waterworks on fears of job cuts.

text.p: A large section of workers at the Manila Waterworks and Sewerage System (MWSS) went on strike on Tuesday on fears many would lose their jobs when the state-owned utility is taken over by private concessionaires next month.

"Almost everybody, about 90 percent of our workers have gone on strike. This is an indefinite walkout. We will not go back to our jobs unless our demands are met," said Elizabeth Nuyad, spokeswoman for the Alliance of MWSS Employees and Supervisors.
The MWSS, which employs 5,700 people, supplies water and maintains the sewage system for 12 million people in Manila.
Water supplies to the city were normal despite the strike but services could be affected if the strike continued, Nuyad said.
MWSS administrator Angel Lazaro was not available for comment but staff in his office said the strike was partial.

Nuyad said MWSS' three unions, which had formed an alliance, were demanding that the new concessionaires do away with a six-month probationary period they had proposed for all employees. The new concessionaires are due to take over the utility's management on August 1.
In January, the government auctioned two 25-year concessions to operate the Manila East and Manila West waterworks.
A consortium of Ayala Corp, Bechtel Corp of the United States and United Utilities won the contract for the east zone. The west zone was won by Benpres Holdings Corp and Lyonnaise des Eaux SA.
